title: C0 vs Faster-GS component matrix (pre-CUDA-modification gate)

baseline.loss: 0.8*L1 + 0.2*(1-SSIM), full-resolution fused SSIM, tile16, seed=42, 30K iters, densification 500..15000, black background

provenance_sha256.note: Local C0_V3_FINAL30K .so/core hashes do NOT match the task-pinned hashes. Likely build-path/toolchain embedding (CUDA extensions embed the build dir path; local build_dir differs from /root/epic05_frozen/...). Provenance gap: authoritative C0 binary/source must be reconciled before any implementation. Does NOT block audit/oracle.

reference.name: Faster-GS: Analyzing and Improving Gaussian Splatting Optimization (CVPR 2026)

classification_legend.ALREADY_IN_C0: C0 already implements an equivalent (exact or superset) mechanism; no port needed.
classification_legend.DISTINCT_AND_EXACT: Faster-GS mechanism is different from C0 but produces identical results (bitwise or algebraically exact); portable in principle.
classification_legend.DISTINCT_BUT_APPROXIMATE: Faster-GS mechanism changes numerics/quality; not an exact systems win under the task's prohibitions.
classification_legend.INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_C0: Cannot be combined with frozen C0 without breaking the research problem.

components.name: Two-stage (depth-based instance/bucket) sorting

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Stage 1: depth-key + touched-tile count per primitive; radix-sort depth keys. Stage 2: create per-tile instance lists + extract instance ranges. Produces depth-correct back-to-front order via instance/bucket buffers.

c0_evidence.summary: gsplat single-pass tile sort: count intersections per tile, exclusive scan, fill flatten_ids. NO instance/bucket structure. Depth-correct back-to-front within each tile.

components.rationale: Both produce identical depth-correct back-to-front rendering; the sort strategy differs (single-pass tile vs two-stage depth-instance). Result-equivalent (exact), not approximate.
components.portability: HIGH-RISK / HIGH-OVERHEAD: requires replacing the entire rasterizer addressing (instance/bucket buffers) and the per-Gaussian backward. Essentially a rasterizer swap.
components.prohibited_shortcut_risk: None inherent, but the coupling to instance/bucket buffers makes surgical porting impractical; a full swap risks changing the research problem.

components.name: Per-Gaussian backward

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Per-Gaussian gradient accumulation over visible instances via bucket structure.

c0_evidence.summary: C0 already computes per-Gaussian gradients (grad_means2D, grad_conic, etc.) with H8_MR + absgrad moments in the backward kernel.

components.rationale: C0's H8_MR backward is already a per-Gaussian backward with absgrad. Faster-GS's bucket-based per-Gaussian backward is a different implementation of the same capability; marginal value is restructuring, not a new capability.
components.portability: N/A (already present). Porting the bucket-based variant would be a rewrite with no exact-win guarantee.

components.name: Opacity-aware / tighter Gaussian bounds (truncation)

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Configurable opacity-interpretation + tighter truncation (1/2/3/4-sigma) with alpha-threshold culling; 1.15x EWA clip.

markers: no opacity-based culling beyond alpha threshold
c0_evidence.summary: C0 uses standard 3-sigma gsplat bounds (eps2d=0.3); no aggressive opacity culling.

components.rationale: With original_opacity_interpretation=true and TRUNCATION_MODE=0 (3.33-sigma) it is ~equivalent to 3DGS. The tighter modes (1/2-sigma) cull more Gaussians and CHANGE rendering/quality. Task prohibits quality-changing truncation as an exact systems improvement.
components.portability: Only the default (3.33-sigma) mode is exact-equivalent, and that is ALREADY_IN_C0-equivalent. The tighter modes are prohibited.
components.prohibited_shortcut_risk: HIGH: tighter-bounds culling changes the research problem (quality); explicitly prohibited.

components.name: Activation fusion (covariance/conic/opacity/color in one kernel)

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Fused preprocess kernel computes covariance, conic, opacity, and color in a single pass.

c0_evidence.summary: C0 already ships fused projection kernels (ProjectionEWA3DGSFused.cu).

components.rationale: C0 already has fused activation/projection. No port needed.

components.name: SH buffer / SH evaluation fusion

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Separate DC (sh_coefficients_0) + rest buffers; fused SH-to-color evaluation with active/total base counts.

c0_evidence.summary: C0 already fuses SH evaluation (sh_coeffs_to_color_fast) with L1+ and view-direction variants.

components.rationale: Both fuse SH evaluation. The DC+rest buffer layout is a memory-layout choice; C0's [N,D] coeff layout is functionally equivalent. No exact-win port.

components.name: Custom fused Adam

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Element-wise fused Adam with bias correction; processes every element; no skipping.

markers: adam_kernel processes all elements (optional per-Gaussian valid mask)
c0_evidence.summary: C0 gsplat fused Adam: all elements, optional valid mask, NO bias correction.

components.rationale: Both are fused Adam over all elements. The delta is bias correction (Faster-GS includes it; C0 omits it). Bias correction is a SEMANTIC optimizer change, not a performance fusion. Task prohibits changing Adam semantics.
components.portability: N/A for the fusion. The bias-correction delta is DISTINCT_BUT_APPROXIMATE/semantics (prohibited to change).
components.prohibited_shortcut_risk: HIGH: adding bias correction changes Adam semantics (prohibited #2). The fusion itself is already in C0.

components.name: Backward -> optimizer fusion (fused bwd+Adam)

faster_gs_evidence.summary: FasterGSFused inlines the Adam update into the per-Gaussian backward kernel, eliminating the separate optimizer kernel and the gradient write/read round-trip.

markers: backward writes grad_* then Adam reads grad_*
c0_evidence.summary: C0 runs backward and Adam as two separate kernels with a gradient tensor round-trip.

components.rationale: Fusing the identical Adam math into the backward kernel is algebraically exact (same update, fused execution) IF the invisible-Gaussian skip is stripped. The shipped FasterGSFused has 'if(primitive_n_touched_tiles==0) return;' (invisible-Gaussian optimizer skipping) which is PROHIBITED; the fusion structure without that skip is the legitimate, exact component.
components.portability: MEDIUM: rewrite the H8_MR backward kernel to inline the Adam update (moments already computed for absgrad), strip the n_touched==0 skip, and re-validate Adam m/v state parity + zero-gradient row parity.
components.prohibited_shortcut_risk: HIGH if shipped as-is: must strip invisible-Gaussian skipping (prohibited #1) and must NOT change zero-gradient Adam semantics (prohibited #2). The fusion must keep bias-correction status identical to C0 (C0 has none).

components.name: Locality-preserving / Morton(Z-order) ordering of Gaussians + optimizer states

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Framework-layer (NeRFICG CudaUtils, NOT the CUDA backend) re-sort of ALL Gaussian params + their optimizer Adam states by Morton code of the means, every 5000 iters until iter 15000. Improves memory locality for subsequent kernels.

markers: no morton/z-order re-sort of params+optimizer states in the training loop
c0_evidence.summary: C0 has NO Morton/Z-order reordering in its densification/training path. The z_order hits in C0 are the gsplat distributed-rendering option, unrelated to training-time locality.

components.rationale: Morton re-sort permutes (param, Adam m, Adam v) rows together by a deterministic key of the means; the multiset of (param,moment) pairs is unchanged, so the training trajectory and result are identical (exact, result-preserving). It is a pure memory-locality optimization.
components.portability: FRAMEWORK-LAYER port (Python/torch): implement morton_encode + a stable argsort + a joint sort of params and optimizer states, mirroring apply_morton_ordering. No CUDA kernel change strictly required, but the optimizer-state migration must be exact.
components.prohibited_shortcut_risk: Must permute param AND exp_avg AND exp_avg_sq rows together (else it changes Adam semantics / breaks zero-gradient rows). Must NOT drop or reorder differently across param groups. Pure permutation => no quality change.

components.name: Frontend allocation / densification memory handling

faster_gs_evidence.summary: Blob-based frontend buffer allocation (single allocation per buffer class) tied to the instance/bucket structure.

c0_evidence.summary: C0 allocates separate tensors per quantity (gsplat style).

components.rationale: Blob-based allocation reduces launch overhead and fragmentation; same data, different allocation strategy (exact). HOWEVER it is tightly coupled to the instance/bucket buffer structure (C1); without C1 there is little to allocate.
components.portability: LOW standalone: benefit is mostly realized alongside C1 (two-stage sort). Per-iteration allocation overhead is small (~0.1-0.3ms).

audit_corrections.reason: Initial grep only scanned the FasterGSCudaBackend/ CUDA sources, where Morton is absent. Full-repo grep found morton_encode/apply_morton_ordering in Model.py + Trainer.py (NeRFICG framework layer, configured by fastergs_garden.yaml MORTON_ORDERING_*).
